decisions.text: Which staging subdomain name — new.marcelioleal.com, staging.marcelioleal.com, or hugo.marcelioleal.com. Resolved: new.marcelioleal.com (short, memorable, naturally retires at cutover) with CNAME at registrar, TTL 300s.

Font choice for the personal visual touch — system sans-serif stack vs hosted pair like Inter + JetBrains Mono. Resolved: system sans-serif stack (no hosted fonts in Phase 1 — zero FOIT/FOUT, no cookie/GDPR exposure, matches minimal reference).

Analytics stack — Plausible, Umami, or none. Resolved: none for Phase 1 (matches minimal reference, zero consent banner, zero script tags). Netlify Web Analytics remains the deferred option when a metric becomes necessary.
Hugo version to pin. Resolved: v0.170.1 (non-extended edition — v0.170.0 removed the extended edition since LibSass was deprecated).
hugo.toml shape — flat at root vs config/_default/. Resolved: flat hugo.toml at repo root for Phase 1; promote to config/_default/ + config/staging/ only when a second environment variable diverges.

WordPress-to-Hugo exporter tool choice — wordpress-to-hugo-exporter plugin, SchumacherFM/wordpress-to-hugo-exporter, or custom script. Resolved: deferred to Phase 2 Content Migration (not relevant for Phase 1 Foundation).

userStories.title: Scaffold greenfield Hugo repository with PaperMod submodule and layered folder structure
userStories.description: As a site maintainer, I want a pristine Hugo + PaperMod repository scaffolded at the project root with the foundation's four-layer folder structure, a minimal bilingual hugo.toml, the PaperMod theme pinned as a shallow submodule, and Hugo 0.170.1 pinned via .tool-versions, so that every subsequent Phase 1 story (i18n, overrides, 404s, CSS, deploy) lands into an already-correct skeleton.
acceptanceCriteria: The repository root at /Users/marcelioleal/workspace/newsite contains an initialized git repository with at least one commit on the `main` branch (observable: `git log --oneline` prints one or more commits and `git branch --show-current` prints `main`).

A flat `hugo.toml` exists at the repo root and declares exactly: `baseURL = "https://new.marcelioleal.com/"`, `title = "Marcelio Leal"`, `theme = "PaperMod"`, `defaultContentLanguage = "pt-br"`, `defaultContentLanguageInSubdir = false`, and two `[languages.*]` blocks — `[languages.pt-br]` with `contentDir = "content/pt-br"` and `weight = 1`, `[languages.en]` with `contentDir = "content/en"` and `weight = 2`. No `[params]` block is emitted by THIS story (story 05 owns params).
A `.gitignore` at repo root contains exactly these four ignore patterns (one per line): `/public/`, `/resources/`, `.hugo_build.lock`, `.DS_Store`.
A `.tool-versions` at repo root contains the single line `hugo 0.170.1` so asdf/mise users resolve the pinned non-extended Hugo binary without additional configuration.

PaperMod is registered as a shallow git submodule at `themes/PaperMod/` pointing at `https://github.com/adityatelange/hugo-PaperMod.git`: `.gitmodules` records the path `themes/PaperMod` and that URL, and `themes/PaperMod/` is checked out with `layouts/_partials/header.html` present on disk (proof the submodule content is initialized, not just referenced).

The eight directory placeholders required by later Phase 1 stories exist on disk and are tracked by git via `.gitkeep` files: `i18n/.gitkeep`, `assets/css/extended/.gitkeep`, `layouts/partials/.gitkeep`, `layouts/_default/.gitkeep`, `static/.gitkeep`, `content/pt-br/.gitkeep`, `content/en/.gitkeep`, `data/.gitkeep`.
`archetypes/default.md` exists as a one-line front-matter template so `hugo new` works out of the box.

`hugo --quiet` runs from the repo root and exits 0, proving the config parses, both language roots are discoverable, and PaperMod resolves as a theme — i.e. the scaffold is build-ready for the next story to drop content and overrides into.
The empty-site `hugo version` reports exactly `hugo v0.170.1` (non-extended), confirming the `.tool-versions` pin binds the local Hugo binary this verify runs under.

`bash -n` on every `.sh` script this story touches exits 0 (there are no shipped shell scripts in this scaffold story, so this check is vacuously satisfied; it is the project's own syntax check because the repo has no typed language in this story's file set).
userStories.notes:
Foundation-entry (greenfield) story. Per the outline's explicit scope narrowing, this story owns ONLY the directory skeleton + hugo.toml skeleton + PaperMod submodule + .gitignore + .tool-versions + git init. CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, netlify.toml, i18n YAML, header override, 404s, CSS, security headers, and deploy wiring are OWNED BY LATER OUTLINE ENTRIES (02-11) and MUST NOT be created here. The foundation proposal's `## CLAUDE.md Draft` and `## AGENTS.md Draft` are intentionally not emitted by this story — the orchestrator split the foundation across 11 entries, and story 10 (`Ship Netlify security headers and repo meta files`) is the natural home for repo meta files. The `.editorconfig` similarly belongs to story 10 or story 08 (Netlify config), not here. Submodule URL `https://github.com/adityatelange/hugo-PaperMod.git` is verbatim from foundation Appendix C. `hugo.toml` fields are the minimal subset of foundation Appendix A that this story's scope needs — the `[params]`, `[markup.goldmark.renderer]`, and `[markup.highlight]` blocks are deferred to story 05 (aesthetic + params) because this story is scaffold-only.

implementation.approach: Per Folder Layout and Appendix C of the foundation proposal: run `git init` + `git branch -M main` at the repo root, then `git submodule add --depth=1 https://github.com/adityatelange/hugo-PaperMod.git themes/PaperMod` followed by `git submodule update --init --recursive`. Author the minimal hugo.toml carrying only the fields this story's scope requires (baseURL, title, theme, defaultContentLanguage, defaultContentLanguageInSubdir, and the two `[languages.*]` blocks) — leave `[params]` and markup blocks to story 05 to avoid duplicating a fact two stories would then each need to keep in sync. Write `.gitignore` and `.tool-versions` verbatim as the acceptance criteria state. `mkdir -p` the eight directory placeholders and `touch` a `.gitkeep` in each so git tracks them (empty directories are invisible to git otherwise). Emit `archetypes/default.md` as a one-line `+++` TOML front-matter stub so `hugo new` works without later retrofit. Finally `git add .` and `git commit -m "chore: phase 1 foundation — Hugo + PaperMod bilingual scaffold (story 01)"`. The commit subject follows the foundation's own English convention (CLAUDE.md § Prose language).

verification.expect: Repository is a git-initialized Hugo site on `main` with the PaperMod submodule checked out, a minimal bilingual hugo.toml, .gitignore and .tool-versions in place, and `hugo --quiet` builds an empty site cleanly with Hugo 0.170.1.

tasks: Run `git init` at `/Users/marcelioleal/workspace/newsite` and `git branch -M main` to create the repo on the correct default branch.
Add PaperMod as a shallow submodule: `git submodule add --depth=1 https://github.com/adityatelange/hugo-PaperMod.git themes/PaperMod`, then `git submodule update --init --recursive`.
Write `.gitignore` with the four patterns `/public/`, `/resources/`, `.hugo_build.lock`, `.DS_Store` (one per line, trailing newline).
Write `.tool-versions` containing the single line `hugo 0.170.1` so asdf/mise users bind the pinned non-extended Hugo.
Write the minimal `hugo.toml` per foundation Appendix A's first six top-level keys plus the two `[languages.*]` blocks ONLY — no `[params]`, no markup blocks (story 05 owns those).

Create the eight directory placeholders via `mkdir -p` and `touch` a `.gitkeep` inside each: `i18n/`, `assets/css/extended/`, `layouts/partials/`, `layouts/_default/`, `static/`, `content/pt-br/`, `content/en/`, `data/`.

Write `archetypes/default.md` as a one-line front-matter stub (`+++
title = '{{ replace .Name "-" " " | title }}'
date = {{ .Date }}
draft = true
+++`) so `hugo new` works for later stories without a retrofit.

Confirm `hugo version` reports `hugo v0.170.1` and `hugo --quiet` exits 0 from the repo root; if the local Hugo binary is not 0.170.1, install via asdf/mise so the `.tool-versions` pin binds before proceeding.

Stage every new file with explicit paths (`git add .gitignore .gitmodules .tool-versions hugo.toml archetypes/ i18n/ assets/ layouts/ static/ content/ data/ themes/PaperMod`) — not `git add .` — to avoid pulling in stray unrelated files.
Create the initial commit: `git commit -m "chore: phase 1 foundation — Hugo + PaperMod bilingual scaffold (story 01)"`.

userStories.title: Author bilingual UI strings and home + about placeholder content
userStories.description: As the site owner (Marcelio), I want pt-br and en UI strings and placeholder home + about pages authored so that the scaffolded Hugo site builds cleanly in both languages with no missing-translation warnings and the orphan-badge contract is in place for the language switcher.
acceptanceCriteria: A visitor requesting / (default pt-br) sees the pt-br home page with its welcome paragraph rendered from content/pt-br/_index.md and /en/ serves the mirrored English home from content/en/_index.md; /about/ and /en/about/ each render a one-paragraph placeholder bio describing Marcelio as writing on tech and personal topics (per resolvedDecisions: do not invent concrete biographical details).

i18n/pt-br.yaml and i18n/en.yaml both exist and both define, at minimum, these snake_case keys (per foundation Naming Conventions § i18n string IDs): site_description, nav_about, only_in_language, switch_to_language, not_found_title, not_found_body, back_to_home. The orphan-badge key is only_in_language (not orphan_badge) because the switcher partial in US-003 and the foundation's CLAUDE.md § 'When modifying the language switcher' both read i18n/<lang>.yaml key only_in_language verbatim; the pt-br value is 'apenas em %s' and the en value is 'only in %s'.

content/pt-br/about/index.md and content/en/about/index.md both carry front-matter with translationKey: "about" (per foundation Module Template § Worked example L126 and L139) so Hugo pairs them as translations and the switcher renders a translation link rather than the orphan badge for the About page.

hugo --quiet --gc --minify exits 0 against the tree with no missing-translation warnings for the two configured default languages (pt-br, en); the build is the structural lint per foundation Lint and Format Config § Decision item 2.

The project's own syntax check passes: every YAML file (i18n/pt-br.yaml, i18n/en.yaml) parses as valid YAML and every Markdown file's YAML front-matter parses cleanly — Hugo's own parser is the authoritative check and is exercised by the build in the previous criterion.
userStories.notes: Orphan-badge key: the outline prompt listed orphan_badge semantically, but the foundation proposal's CLAUDE.md § 'When modifying the language switcher' pins the actual YAML key as only_in_language and that is what US-003's header partial will read. Using only_in_language here keeps the cross-story contract intact. The pt-br home + about copy must stay neutral per resolvedDecisions — one welcome paragraph on each home page and a one-liner bio on each about page, no invented biographical facts.

implementation.approach: Author the two i18n YAML files with identical snake_case key sets (per Naming Conventions § i18n string IDs); use %s as the Hugo i18n printf placeholder in only_in_language for the switcher's language-name substitution. Author each _index.md with minimal front-matter (title, date) plus a short welcome paragraph. For the two About bundles, use the verbatim front-matter template from foundation § Module Template (title, date, draft: false, translationKey: "about") so Hugo pairs the two as translations and the switcher renders a link rather than the orphan badge. Keep all copy neutral per resolvedDecisions — a one-liner bio about writing on tech and personal topics, no invented facts.
implementation.verify: set -euo pipefail && test -f i18n/pt-br.yaml && test -f i18n/en.yaml && test -f content/pt-br/_index.md && test -f content/pt-br/about/index.md && test -f content/en/_index.md && test -f content/en/about/index.md && python3 -c "import yaml; p=yaml.safe_load(open('i18n/pt-br.yaml')); e=yaml.safe_load(open('i18n/en.yaml')); req={'site_description','nav_about','only_in_language','switch_to_language','not_found_title','not_found_body','back_to_home'}; mp=req-set(p.keys()); me=req-set(e.keys()); assert not mp, f'pt-br.yaml missing: {mp}'; assert not me, f'en.yaml missing: {me}'; assert '%s' in p['only_in_language'] and '%s' in e['only_in_language'], 'only_in_language must contain %s printf placeholder'" && grep -q 'translationKey:[[:space:]]*"about"' content/pt-br/about/index.md && grep -q 'translationKey:[[:space:]]*"about"' content/en/about/index.md && hugo --quiet --gc --minify 2>&1 | tee /tmp/hugo-build.log && ! grep -i 'missing translation\|WARN' /tmp/hugo-build.log

verification.expect: hugo --quiet --gc --minify builds both languages cleanly; all 6 content/i18n files exist; both YAML files define the required 7 keys; About bundles share translationKey "about" so the switcher renders a link rather than the orphan badge.

userStories.title: Override header partial with orphan-aware bilingual language switcher
userStories.description: As a bilingual site visitor, I want a visible language switcher in the site header that honestly tells me when a page has no translation so that I never click a link that silently takes me to the wrong page or home.
acceptanceCriteria: A visitor on any PT or EN page sees a header language switcher that renders one entry per site language by iterating site.Languages (not site.Home.Translations), so the inactive language is always present in the DOM — PaperMod's default partial hides orphans by iterating .Translations and is explicitly rejected here.
For the CURRENT language, the switcher renders a <span aria-current="true"> containing the language display name (from .Language.LanguageName), with no <a> element — it is not clickable.

For the OTHER language WHEN the current page has a translation in that language (branch on .AllTranslations / .IsTranslated), the switcher renders a single <a href="{{ .Permalink }}"> whose href is taken from the matching .Translations entry, carries an aria-label built from the i18n string switch_to_language interpolated with the target language display name, and is keyboard-focusable with a visible focus outline (no outline: none; outline:auto or an explicit visible focus style is applied in CSS or inline on :focus-visible).

For the OTHER language WHEN the current page has NO translation, the switcher renders a non-link <span class="lang-badge" aria-disabled="true"> whose visible text is the i18n string only_in_language interpolated with the target language display name (e.g. "Only in PT" / "Somente em EN"), so the orphan state is honest and announced to assistive tech.

The header nav includes an "About" entry whose visible text comes from the i18n key nav_about and whose href is /about/ on the PT site and /en/about/ on the EN site, resolved through the site's language-aware URL helpers (relLangURL or equivalent), NOT hardcoded.

The switcher works with JavaScript disabled: viewing source after `hugo --quiet` shows the three branches rendered as pure HTML with no inline onclick, no x-data, no requestAnimationFrame, no redirect script.

The override lives at layouts/partials/header.html (site-root), NOT at themes/PaperMod/layouts/partials/header.html — Hugo's lookup order resolves the site-root partial first, leaving the vendored theme untouched; `test -f layouts/partials/header.html && ! test -f themes/PaperMod/layouts/partials/header.html` holds, or the theme file is preserved verbatim as vendored.
`hugo --quiet` exits 0 with no template errors from the newly authored partial.
Bash syntax check passes: `bash -n` on any shell helpers is irrelevant here; the project's own build check is `hugo --quiet` and it succeeds.
userStories.notes: verification.strategy is 'visual' because the orphan-badge case needs eyeball confirmation that the disabled state is visually distinguishable; story 11 is the full visual verification gate and will re-check this end-to-end. The MH-4 template under E-3 in best-practices.md is the authoritative shape — follow it rather than inventing a parallel structure.

implementation.approach: Author layouts/partials/header.html from scratch as a site-root override (Hugo lookup order resolves this before themes/PaperMod/layouts/partials/header.html, so the vendored theme is untouched per the foundation proposal's Layering section). Follow the MH-4 verbatim template under E-3 in .aimi/research/2026-11-21-wordpress-to-hugo-migration-phase-1-foundation-134302-best-practices.md: iterate `{{ range site.Languages }}`, compare `{{ if eq . site.Language }}` for the current branch, else walk `{{ range $.AllTranslations }}` (or check `.IsTranslated` and index .Translations by language code) to decide link-vs-badge. Pull visible strings through `{{ i18n "switch_to_language" . }}`, `{{ i18n "orphan_badge" . }}`, and `{{ i18n "nav_about" }}` so copy stays in i18n/pt-br.yaml and i18n/en.yaml (produced by US-002). Render the About nav entry with `{{ absLangURL "about/" }}` or `{{ "about/" | relLangURL }}` so Hugo computes /about/ for PT and /en/about/ for EN without hardcoding. Keep the markup semantic: a single <nav> wrapping an <ul> of <li>, with the switcher as sibling <li>s; aria-current="true" on the active span, aria-disabled="true" on the orphan span, aria-label on the inter-language <a>. Do NOT add JS; the switcher is pure HTML so it works with JS off. Visible focus is covered by not suppressing :focus outlines — leave the browser default or let story 05's aesthetic CSS add a :focus-visible rule.
implementation.verify: set -euo pipefail; test -f layouts/partials/header.html; grep -q 'site.Languages' layouts/partials/header.html; grep -q 'AllTranslations\|\.Translations' layouts/partials/header.html; grep -q 'aria-current' layouts/partials/header.html; grep -q 'aria-disabled' layouts/partials/header.html; grep -q 'switch_to_language' layouts/partials/header.html; grep -q 'only_in_language' layouts/partials/header.html; grep -q 'nav_about' layouts/partials/header.html; ! grep -q 'onclick=' layouts/partials/header.html; ! grep -q 'x-data' layouts/partials/header.html; hugo --quiet

verification.expect: On the PT home, the header shows an aria-current PT indicator and an EN link (because the home is translated). Navigate to a PT-only post: the EN side renders as an aria-disabled 'Somente em EN' / 'Only in EN' badge, not a link. The About link reads 'Sobre' on PT and 'About' on EN and routes to /about/ and /en/about/ respectively. Tab to the EN link: a visible focus outline appears. Disable JS in the browser and reload: the switcher still renders and still behaves as described.

tasks: Create layouts/partials/header.html as a new file (site-root override; do not touch themes/PaperMod/layouts/partials/header.html)
Scaffold a <header> with a <nav><ul> structure containing the About link and the language-switcher region

Render the About entry as
  • {{ i18n "nav_about" }}
    • so PT resolves /about/ and EN resolves /en/about/
Add the switcher loop: {{ range site.Languages }} — iterate every configured language, not .Translations
Inside the loop, branch on {{ if eq . site.Language }} and render {{ .LanguageName }} for the current language
For the else branch, test membership against $.AllTranslations (or .IsTranslated + index .Translations by .Lang) to decide link-vs-badge
When a translation exists, emit {{ .LanguageName }}
When no translation exists, emit {{ i18n "only_in_language" . }}
Confirm no JavaScript, no x-data, no onclick, no redirect script was introduced; the switcher is pure HTML
Run `hugo --quiet` locally and confirm it exits 0 with no template errors
Run `hugo server` and manually confirm the PT and EN branches render as described in verification.expect — covered end-to-end by story 11's exit verification

userStories.title: Ship per-language 404 pages with inline language-detection script
userStories.description: As a visitor landing on an unresolved URL, I want a bilingual 404 page that recovers to my language so that I can find my way home whether I hit /does-not-exist or /en/does-not-exist, with or without JavaScript enabled.
acceptanceCriteria:
A visitor hitting any unresolved URL under / lands on a 404 page whose body contains both the pt-br message and the en message wrapped in

and

respectively, with recovery links to / (Início) and to /en/ (Home), so both language audiences self-recover.

With JavaScript enabled, the inline <script> in layouts/404.html hides the pt-br paragraph when location.pathname.startsWith('/en/') and otherwise hides the en paragraph; with JavaScript disabled both paragraphs remain visible (graceful degradation). The script runs synchronously before paint without requiring any external asset.

Hugo's per-language 404 suffix convention is honoured: the 404 templates live at layouts/404.html, layouts/404.pt-br.html and layouts/404.en.html (NOT under layouts/_default/ and NOT as content/404.md), so Hugo emits public/404.html and public/en/404.html on build (Hugo 404 template reference, framework-docs § C10).

layouts/404.pt-br.html and layouts/404.en.html each render a single-language 404 using the i18n keys not_found_title, not_found_body and back_to_home via {{ i18n "<key>" }}, consuming the strings authored by US-002 in i18n/pt-br.yaml and i18n/en.yaml.

Each of the three templates emits a top-level nav link back to the site root for its language (pt-br templates link to / and /en templates link to /en/) using either the PaperMod header partial via {{ partial "header.html" . }} when the partial renders in a 404 context, or a minimal inline <nav> when it does not — never leaving the visitor without a reachable home link.

hugo --quiet (Hugo 0.170.1 as pinned in .tool-versions) builds the site without error and produces both public/404.html (Netlify's single catch-all 404 handler) and public/en/404.html (per-language 404 reachable via the Netlify redirect rule planned for US-008).
Hugo's own syntax check passes: `hugo --quiet` exits 0 with no template parse errors across the three 404 templates.
userStories.notes: Netlify serves only the top-level /404.html as its single catch-all; per-language routing to /en/404.html is wired by a redirect rule planned for US-008 (netlify.toml). This story only authors the templates; the end-to-end visual walkthrough with JS on/off at mobile and desktop widths is gated by US-011.

implementation.approach:
Three Hugo templates at the site-root layouts/ (never under _default/, per framework-docs § C10). layouts/404.html is the bilingual fallback (Netlify's catch-all): render

404

, then

Página não encontrada.

and

Page not found.

, then bilingual recovery links to / and /en/, then a small inline

End-to-end acceptance is gated by US-011.

userStories.title: Lock staging noindex via robots.txt and conditional meta-robots head injection
userStories.description: As a site operator, I want staging (new.marcelioleal.com) to emit robots.txt Disallow:/ and meta robots noindex,nofollow so search engines never index the preview environment while apex production can later flip to index,follow.
acceptanceCriteria: A visitor loading https://new.marcelioleal.com/robots.txt sees `User-agent: *` on one line and `Disallow: /` on the next, and viewing the rendered homepage source on staging shows `<meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow">` inside <head>, so Google and Bing crawlers decline to index any staging page (resolves AC-new-1, AC-new-2 from spec-flow).

static/robots.txt exists at the repository root and its exact body is the two lines `User-agent: *` followed by `Disallow: /` (terminating newline permitted); Hugo copies it verbatim into public/robots.txt on build.

layouts/partials/extend_head.html exists and contains a conditional Hugo template block that emits `<meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow">` when `hugo.Environment` equals `preview` or `staging`, OR when `.Site.BaseURL` contains the literal `new.marcelioleal.com` (belt-and-suspenders), and emits nothing otherwise.

Building with `HUGO_ENV=preview hugo` writes the noindex meta into public/index.html; building with `HUGO_ENV=production hugo` writes a public/index.html containing no `noindex` token anywhere, so the apex production deploy (Phase 3) is free to be indexed.
The project's own syntax check passes: `hugo --quiet` exits 0 with no template-parse errors against the new extend_head.html partial.
userStories.notes:
This story CREATES layouts/partials/extend_head.html with only the noindex conditional block. Story 07 (SEO head) will APPEND canonical, hreflang, and OpenGraph tags to the SAME file — do not duplicate the partial, extend it. PaperMod auto-includes extend_head.html inside <head>, so no base template changes are required here. The two-condition guard (hugo.Environment check PLUS BaseURL substring match) is intentional belt-and-suspenders: a misconfigured Netlify deploy context that fails to set HUGO_ENV still gets blocked by the staging host match.

userStories.title: Emit canonical, hreflang alternates, and Open Graph defaults in extend_head.html
userStories.description: As a site owner publishing bilingual pages, I want every rendered page to emit a self-canonical link, pt-br/en/x-default hreflang alternates, and Open Graph defaults so that search engines index the correct language variant and social shares show a consistent preview.
acceptanceCriteria: Loading / in the browser shows an HTML head block that contains a self-canonical link, hreflang alternates for pt-br, en, and x-default, and Open Graph defaults (og:title, og:description, og:type, og:locale, og:locale:alternate, og:image, og:url) — the preview matches when the page URL is pasted into a link-unfurling tool.
layouts/partials/extend_head.html (appended to the file story 06 created) emits <link rel="canonical" href="{{ .Permalink }}"> on every page.

layouts/partials/extend_head.html iterates site.Languages and emits <link rel="alternate" hreflang="pt-br" href="..."> and <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="..."> pointing at the sibling page URL resolved through .AllTranslations / .Translations (per spec-flow G-2, backed by Hugo .Translations / .IsTranslated).
layouts/partials/extend_head.html emits <link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="..."> pointing at the pt-br variant (site.Home for defaultContentLanguage=pt-br).

Open Graph defaults are written using site title, page .Description (falling back to .Site.Params.description), og:type=website for the home and article for leaf pages, og:locale=pt_BR or en_US derived from the current page language, og:locale:alternate for the other language, og:image set via absURL to /og-default.png, and og:url set to .Permalink (spec-flow G-3, AC-new-4).
static/og-default.png exists as a non-empty valid PNG placeholder sized 1200x630 — the file silences PaperMod's default-OG-image fallback and loads when fetched directly from the rendered site.

static/favicon.ico exists as a non-empty valid ICO placeholder (minimum 16x16) referenced by Hugo's default favicon convention — a browser request for /favicon.ico returns the file rather than a 404 (AC-new-5).

hugo.toml contains, under [params], description = "Marcelio Leal's personal site — pt-br default, bilingual" (used as og:description fallback) and images = ["og-default.png"] (PaperMod default-OG-image hint).

hugo --quiet builds without missing-translation warnings and the rendered public/index.html contains all of: rel="canonical", hreflang="pt-br", hreflang="en", hreflang="x-default", og:title, og:image, and a reference to og-default.png or favicon.

userStories.notes: Placeholder binaries (og-default.png 1200x630, favicon.ico 16x16) are generated at execute time without external tools: tasks[] directs the executor to use Python's built-in base64 decode of a known-good minimal PNG/ICO byte stream, or `python3 -c` with struct to write a solid-color PNG. Example recipe recorded in tasks[] — the files only need to be valid, non-empty, and the correct MIME; visual fidelity is not asserted by this story. hugo.toml `description` and `images` params are appended only if not already present (idempotent).

userStories.title: Configure Netlify build with pinned Hugo version and context-aware baseURL
userStories.description: As the site operator, I want a netlify.toml that pins the Hugo toolchain and sets baseURL per deploy context so every Netlify environment (production, deploy-preview, branch-deploy) builds reproducibly with the correct absolute URLs without hardcoding them in hugo.toml.
acceptanceCriteria: A reviewer opening netlify.toml at the repository root reads a single build configuration that pins Hugo 0.170.1, sets the Sao Paulo timezone, enables recursive submodule checkout for the PaperMod theme consumed from US-001, and declares three deploy contexts (production, deploy-preview, branch-deploy) each rebuilding Hugo with its own absolute baseURL sourced from Netlify's URL and DEPLOY_PRIME_URL environment variables so no absolute domain is baked into hugo.toml.

netlify.toml exists at the repository root and contains these verbatim segments: [build] with command = "hugo --gc --minify" and publish = "public"; [build.environment] with HUGO_VERSION = "0.170.1", TZ = "America/Sao_Paulo", and GIT_SUBMODULE_STRATEGY = "recursive"; [context.production] with command = "hugo --gc --minify --baseURL ${URL}" and environment = { HUGO_ENV = "production" }; [context.deploy-preview] with command = "hugo --gc --minify --baseURL ${DEPLOY_PRIME_URL}" and environment = { HUGO_ENV = "preview" }; [context.branch-deploy] with command = "hugo --gc --minify --baseURL ${DEPLOY_PRIME_URL}" and environment = { HUGO_ENV = "preview" }.

The locally installed Hugo binary reports v0.170.1, matching the pinned HUGO_VERSION, and a quiet local Hugo build completes without error, confirming the hugo.toml + PaperMod submodule from US-001 can be built with the same toolchain Netlify will run.

hugo.toml's baseURL remains a local-dev placeholder (e.g. http://localhost:1313/) and never carries a production hostname, because the [context.*] command overrides inject --baseURL per deploy context; grepping netlify.toml confirms no production hostname is hardcoded there either.

bash -n netlify.toml is not applicable (TOML, not shell); instead, the file is syntactically valid TOML as confirmed by python3 -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open('netlify.toml','rb'))" exiting zero.
userStories.notes: Netlify's 'Git submodules' Site setting is a one-time console toggle done in US-009 at deploy time — netlify.toml alone cannot enable it, but GIT_SUBMODULE_STRATEGY="recursive" in [build.environment] is the companion env var that takes effect once the Site setting is on. This story only authors the config file; it does not execute any deploy. Research anchors: .aimi/research/2026-11-21-wordpress-to-hugo-migration-phase-1-foundation-134302-framework-docs.md §C8-C9 and .aimi/research/2026-11-21-wordpress-to-hugo-migration-phase-1-foundation-134302-best-practices.md §MH-2, §MH-6, §E-2.

implementation.approach: Author a new netlify.toml at the repo root with four TOML tables in this order: [build] (command + publish), [build.environment] (HUGO_VERSION, TZ, GIT_SUBMODULE_STRATEGY), and three [context.*] blocks (production, deploy-preview, branch-deploy) each overriding command with --baseURL and setting an inline environment table for HUGO_ENV. Use the verbatim strings specified in the research's E-2 netlify.toml recipe — do not paraphrase keys or values. baseURL interpolation uses Netlify's own ${URL} (production custom domain) and ${DEPLOY_PRIME_URL} (preview/branch deploy URL) env vars, which Netlify substitutes into the build command before invoking Hugo — this is the per-context baseURL pattern from MH-6 and is the reason hugo.toml's baseURL stays a localhost placeholder. The recursive submodule env var complements (does not replace) the Netlify UI 'Git submodules' toggle flipped in US-009.

verification.expect: netlify.toml exists at the repo root, parses as valid TOML, pins HUGO_VERSION=0.170.1 with TZ=America/Sao_Paulo and GIT_SUBMODULE_STRATEGY=recursive, declares the three deploy contexts each wiring --baseURL to the right Netlify env var (${URL} for production, ${DEPLOY_PRIME_URL} for deploy-preview and branch-deploy) with HUGO_ENV=production or HUGO_ENV=preview as appropriate, contains no hardcoded production hostname, and the local Hugo v0.170.1 toolchain builds the site cleanly.

userStories.title: Deploy to Netlify and wire new.marcelioleal.com staging subdomain
userStories.description: As the site operator, I want to deploy the newsite repository to Netlify behind new.marcelioleal.com so that the migrated Hugo site is reachable over HTTPS on a staging subdomain while the apex marcelioleal.com continues to serve WordPress until Phase 3.
acceptanceCriteria: Operator visits https://new.marcelioleal.com/ in a browser and the Hugo home page renders with language switcher and PT-BR content; navigating to http://new.marcelioleal.com/ is redirected (301 or 308) to the https:// equivalent.

GitHub repository `newsite` exists under the operator's account, `origin` points to `github.com:<user>/newsite.git`, and `main` has been pushed; Netlify has imported that repo and the first production build on `main` finished with status green.

Netlify Site settings -> Build & deploy -> Continuous Deployment has `Git submodules` ENABLED (this one-time console toggle is required because netlify.toml cannot set it; without it, the `themes/` submodule is not checked out at build time and the build fails).

In Netlify Site settings -> Domain management, `new.marcelioleal.com` is listed as a custom domain and its status shows HTTPS active (Let's Encrypt certificate provisioned); at the registrar holding `marcelioleal.com`, a DNS record `new 300 IN CNAME <netlify-subdomain>.netlify.app.` is present with TTL 300s, and no CAA record blocks Let's Encrypt issuance.
The apex domain `marcelioleal.com` DNS records are unchanged in this story and continue to point at the existing WordPress host; only the `new` subdomain is added. (Phase 3 cuts the apex.)

Dry local sanity command succeeds in the repo and writes the expected output: `test -f netlify.toml && hugo --quiet --baseURL "https://new.marcelioleal.com/" --gc --minify && test -f public/index.html`.
`bash -n` on any shell snippets this story introduces passes (there are no shell files committed by this story; the check applies to the verify script itself).
userStories.notes: Operator story. No files are written to the repository by this story; all changes happen in external systems (GitHub, Netlify dashboard, DNS registrar). The repo-side preconditions (`netlify.toml` from US-008, `.gitmodules` from US-001) are already in place. Netlify's Git submodules toggle must be enabled in the console even though netlify.toml exists - the setting is per-site and lives outside the repo config. TTL 300s on the CNAME is chosen so that a bad cutover can be rolled back within minutes.

implementation.approach: Operator workflow executed from a terminal + the Netlify and registrar dashboards. Sequence: (1) create GitHub repo `newsite` under the operator's account, set as `origin`, push `main`; (2) in Netlify, Add new site -> Import from Git -> pick `newsite`; Netlify reads `netlify.toml` from US-008 for build command, publish dir, and HUGO_VERSION; (3) toggle Site settings -> Build & deploy -> Continuous Deployment -> Git submodules ON (one-time, console-only); (4) wait for first production build to finish green; (5) Site settings -> Domain management -> Add custom domain `new.marcelioleal.com`, choose Netlify's DNS-only option (no apex nameserver transfer); (6) at the registrar for `marcelioleal.com`, add `new 300 IN CNAME <netlify-subdomain>.netlify.app.`, clear any blocking CAA record; (7) wait 5-60 minutes for Let's Encrypt provisioning; (8) verify https:// serves and http:// redirects. The local `verify` segment reproduces Netlify's production build command against the repo to catch build-breaking regressions before they reach Netlify.
implementation.verify: set -euo pipefail; test -f netlify.toml; git remote -v | grep -q 'github.com[:/].*newsite'; hugo --quiet --baseURL "https://new.marcelioleal.com/" --gc --minify; test -f public/index.html

verification.expect: Home page renders with the language switcher and PT-BR content visible; requesting http://new.marcelioleal.com/ returns a redirect to https://new.marcelioleal.com/.

gate.prompt: Confirm the following steps are complete: (1) github.com/<user>/newsite exists and `main` is pushed; (2) Netlify site is created and the first production build is green; (3) Netlify Site settings -> Git submodules is ENABLED; (4) new.marcelioleal.com is added as a custom domain in Netlify; (5) the CNAME record exists at the registrar with TTL 300s and no CAA record blocks Let's Encrypt; (6) https://new.marcelioleal.com/ serves the home page AND http:// redirects to https://.

tasks: Create a public GitHub repository named `newsite` under the operator's account via the GitHub UI or `gh repo create`.
Add the GitHub repo as `origin` with `git remote add origin git@github.com:<user>/newsite.git` and push with `git push -u origin main`.
In Netlify, use Add new site -> Import from Git and select the `newsite` repository; let Netlify auto-detect `netlify.toml` from US-008.
In Netlify Site settings -> Build & deploy -> Continuous Deployment, enable the `Git submodules` toggle (one-time; required for the Hugo theme submodule from US-001 to be checked out).
Trigger (or let Netlify trigger) the first production build on `main`; confirm the deploy status is green and note the Netlify-assigned `<name>.netlify.app` subdomain.
In Netlify Site settings -> Domain management, add `new.marcelioleal.com` as a custom domain using the DNS-only option (do not transfer apex nameservers).

At the registrar for `marcelioleal.com`, add `new 300 IN CNAME <name>.netlify.app.` and remove any CAA record that would block Let's Encrypt issuance; leave all other records (including the apex) untouched.
Wait for Let's Encrypt provisioning (5-60 minutes); in Netlify Domain management, confirm HTTPS shows active for new.marcelioleal.com.
In a browser, open https://new.marcelioleal.com/ and verify the home page renders with the language switcher and PT-BR content; verify http://new.marcelioleal.com/ redirects to the https:// URL.
Run the local sanity check from the repo: `test -f netlify.toml && hugo --quiet --baseURL "https://new.marcelioleal.com/" --gc --minify && test -f public/index.html`.

userStories.title: Ship Netlify security headers and repo meta files
userStories.description: As a site operator, I want Netlify to emit a strict baseline of security headers and the repo to carry a complete README plus a pinned Hugo toolchain, so every page served from the migrated site ships with CSP/Referrer/Nosniff/Permissions protection and any contributor can clone, build, and deploy without tribal knowledge.
acceptanceCriteria: A visitor loading any page on the Netlify-served site receives HTTP response headers that set Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, and Permissions-Policy, so the browser enforces the baseline origin/sniffing/permissions posture the migration committed to (AC-new-6).

static/_headers exists at repo root and contains, for the path pattern '/*', all of these literal directives (verbatim): 'Content-Security-Policy: default-src '\''self'\''; img-src '\''self'\'' data: https:; style-src '\''self'\'' '\''unsafe-inline'\''; script-src '\''self'\'' '\''unsafe-inline'\''; font-src '\''self'\''; connect-src '\''self'\''', 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin', 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff', and 'Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), interest-cohort=()'.

README.md exists at repo root and covers, each in its own passage: cloning the repo with recursive submodule init ('git clone ... && git submodule update --init --recursive'), running local dev with 'hugo server -D' at http://localhost:1313/, updating PaperMod via 'git submodule update --remote --merge themes/PaperMod' followed by a manual eyeball before commit, the deploy flow (pushing to main triggers Netlify production build; PRs get deploy previews), and that the Hugo version is pinned via .tool-versions (mise/asdf compatible).
.tool-versions at repo root pins 'hugo 0.170.1', matching the Hugo version declared in netlify.toml, so mise/asdf users and Netlify's build image converge on the same toolchain (AC-new-8).
'hugo --quiet' completes with exit 0 from a clean clone whose submodules have been initialized, proving neither the new _headers file nor the README change breaks the site build.
'hugo --quiet' exits 0 (this project ships no TypeScript or language-level typecheck; the Hugo build is the project's own syntax/consistency check for content and config).
userStories.notes: CSP intentionally allows 'unsafe-inline' in script-src because PaperMod's 404 page ships an inline language-detection script; tightening to a nonce- or hash-based policy would require patching the theme and is out of scope for Phase 1. Permissions-Policy includes 'interest-cohort=()' to opt out of FLoC-style cohort tracking. The .tool-versions file was authored by US-001 pinning hugo 0.170.1; this story only confirms its presence and version string, and re-authors it with the same value if (and only if) it is missing.

implementation.approach: Create static/_headers as a Netlify custom-headers file using the path-prefix syntax (one '/*' block containing four indented header lines); Hugo copies anything under static/ into public/ verbatim at build time, so the file lands at the site root and Netlify applies it to every response. Author README.md as a plain Markdown document with sections for Clone, Local development, Updating the theme, Deploy, and Toolchain, so a new contributor can follow it top-to-bottom. Confirm .tool-versions carries 'hugo 0.170.1' on its own line (asdf/mise format: one 'tool version' pair per line); if US-001's file is already present and correct, leave it unchanged.
implementation.verify: set -euo pipefail; test -f static/_headers; test -f README.md; test -f .tool-versions; grep -q "Content-Security-Policy" static/_headers; grep -q "X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff" static/_headers; grep -q "Referrer-Policy:" static/_headers; grep -q "Permissions-Policy:" static/_headers; grep -q "default-src 'self'" static/_headers; grep -q "img-src 'self' data: https:" static/_headers; grep -q "interest-cohort=()" static/_headers; grep -q "^hugo 0.170.1$" .tool-versions; grep -q "0.170.1" netlify.toml; grep -q "git submodule update --init" README.md; grep -q "hugo server -D" README.md; grep -q "git submodule update --remote --merge themes/PaperMod" README.md; grep -q "Netlify" README.md; grep -q ".tool-versions" README.md; hugo --quiet

verification.expect: static/_headers, README.md, and .tool-versions are present with the required directives, submodule/dev/deploy instructions, and pinned Hugo 0.170.1; 'hugo --quiet' builds the site cleanly.

tasks: Create static/_headers with a single '/*' path block containing the four security headers verbatim as specified by AC-new-6
Author README.md at repo root with Clone (with recursive submodules), Local dev (hugo server -D), Updating PaperMod, Deploy (Netlify main + PR previews), and Toolchain (.tool-versions) sections
Open .tool-versions and confirm the exact line 'hugo 0.170.1' is present; if the file is missing, create it with that single line
Cross-check .tool-versions against netlify.toml to confirm both pin Hugo 0.170.1 (AC-new-8)
Run 'hugo --quiet' from the repo root and confirm exit 0 to prove the new static file is copied to public/ and the build is clean
Run the full verify segment list to confirm every grep anchor matches on the pre-commit tree

userStories.title: Phase 1 exit verification: end-to-end bilingual + a11y + staging checklist
userStories.description: As the migration owner, I want a recorded end-to-end walk-through of the staging deployment so that Phase 1 closes only when all four roadmap success criteria and criteria A-M are confirmed on https://new.marcelioleal.com/.
acceptanceCriteria: Walking https://new.marcelioleal.com/ in a browser renders the PT home as a single-column ~720px layout on a light background in a system sans-serif font, the switcher is visible, and the walk-through is recorded as the gate's observed outcome.
Roadmap Phase 1 success criterion 1 is reaffirmed: the staging subdomain serves a single-column, sans-serif, light-background Hugo site inspired by eltonminetto.dev.
Roadmap Phase 1 success criterion 2 is reaffirmed: Hugo native i18n is configured with content/pt-br and content/en and a visible language switcher is present on home and about in both languages.

Roadmap Phase 1 success criterion 3 is reaffirmed: home and about render in both PT and EN at https://new.marcelioleal.com/, https://new.marcelioleal.com/en/, https://new.marcelioleal.com/sobre/, and https://new.marcelioleal.com/en/about/.

Roadmap Phase 1 success criterion 4 is reaffirmed: when a content page exists in only one language the switcher shows an only-in-PT or only-in-EN badge (disabled, no redirect) rather than hiding or redirecting away.

Criteria A-M are each walked and recorded with a pass/fail note: A home PT at /, B home EN at /en/ with nav labels swapped and switcher offering PT as alternate, C about PT at /sobre/, D about EN at /en/about/, E PT 404 at /does-not-exist/ (both language paragraphs visible with JS off; PT visible and EN hidden with JS on), F EN 404 at /en/does-not-exist/, G orphan-translation case shows disabled only-in-PT/EN badge with no redirect, H `curl -s https://new.marcelioleal.com/robots.txt | grep -q 'Disallow: /'` succeeds, I `curl -sI https://new.marcelioleal.com/` shows HSTS and CSP headers, J view-source on home confirms rel=canonical, hreflang alternates for pt-br and en and x-default, and og:title and og:image, K with JS disabled the switcher links still work and the 404 remains readable with both paragraphs visible, L at 375px mobile width content is legible, the switcher stays visible and there is no horizontal scroll, M keyboard-tabbing through nav and switcher shows a visible focus outline.
The repo-local smoke checks in `implementation.verify` all pass, confirming the files behind criteria A-M are still present and `hugo --quiet` builds the site cleanly.
`bash -n` passes on the inline verify script (the project is bash-only; no typed build step applies to this gate story).
userStories.notes: This is a verification gate story — its deliverable is the recorded walk-through captured against the gate prompt, not code. The `verify` block runs repo-local smoke assertions so a later regression that deletes a required file or breaks the Hugo build is caught locally, but the authoritative check for Phase 1 exit is the manual walk-through recorded via the `gate` field. Any failure in A-M or in any of the four roadmap success criteria blocks closing Phase 1.

implementation.approach: This story closes Phase 1 via a human walk-through of staging at https://new.marcelioleal.com/, recorded against the `gate` prompt below. The agent does not change code; it only runs the repo-local smoke checks in `verify` to confirm the files that back criteria A-M still exist and the site still builds, and then waits on the gate. The walk-through itself traverses the seven URLs listed in A-F plus the orphan-translation case in G, runs the two `curl` assertions in H and I against the live staging host, view-sources the home per J, toggles JS off in DevTools for E and K, resizes to 375px for L, and keyboard-tabs the nav and switcher for M. Each of criteria A-M and each of the four roadmap success criteria is recorded with a pass/fail note before the gate option is selected.
implementation.verify:
set -euo pipefail
test -f layouts/partials/header.html
test -f layouts/partials/extend_head.html
test -f layouts/404.html
test -f static/robots.txt
test -f netlify.toml
grep -q 'Disallow: /' static/robots.txt
grep -qE "rel=[\"']alternate[\"']" layouts/partials/extend_head.html
grep -q 'canonical' layouts/partials/extend_head.html
grep -qE 'orphan|aria-disabled' layouts/partials/header.html
hugo --quiet

verification.expect: All four Phase 1 roadmap success criteria and criteria A-M are confirmed on the staging deployment; any failure blocks closing Phase 1.

gate.prompt: Walk the Phase 1 staging deployment end-to-end per acceptance criteria A-M on https://new.marcelioleal.com/. Reaffirm all four roadmap success criteria (single-column light sans-serif site; Hugo i18n with pt-br and en and a visible switcher; home and about in both languages; orphan-translation shows only-in-PT/EN badge). Any failure blocks closing Phase 1.

tasks: Run the repo-local smoke checks in implementation.verify and confirm all five files exist, robots.txt disallows /, extend_head.html declares rel=alternate and canonical, header.html carries the orphan/aria-disabled marker, and hugo --quiet builds cleanly
Walk criterion A: load https://new.marcelioleal.com/ and record whether PT home renders single-column ~720px on a light background in system sans-serif with the switcher visible
Walk criteria B, C, D: load /en/, /sobre/, /en/about/ in turn and record that EN home swaps nav labels and offers PT in the switcher, PT about renders, and EN about renders
Walk criteria E and F: load /does-not-exist/ with JS off then on and confirm both-paragraphs visible then PT-only; load /en/does-not-exist/ and confirm the EN 404 renders
Walk criterion G: identify or stage an orphan-translation content page and confirm the switcher shows the only-in-PT/EN disabled badge with no redirect
Walk criteria H and I: run curl -s https://new.marcelioleal.com/robots.txt | grep -q 'Disallow: /' and curl -sI https://new.marcelioleal.com/ and confirm HSTS and CSP headers are present
Walk criterion J: view-source on the home and confirm rel=canonical, hreflang alternates for pt-br and en and x-default, and og:title and og:image tags

Walk criteria K, L, M: disable JS in DevTools and confirm switcher links still navigate and the 404 remains readable; resize to 375px and confirm legibility with no horizontal scroll; keyboard-tab through nav and switcher and confirm a visible focus outline
Reaffirm each of the four roadmap Phase 1 success criteria against the recorded walk-through and record a pass note for each
Resolve the gate: select 'All criteria A-M pass' only when every criterion and all four roadmap success criteria passed; otherwise select 'Blocked - list failures' and list each failure
